topic: Task-Based versus Thread-Based: Leveraging Modern Schedulers
explanation: Task-based concurrency (using `std::async`) is the preferred approach because it automatically reaps the benefits of modern standard library implementations, which often employ state-of-the-art thread schedulers, system-wide thread pools, and work-stealing algorithms for optimized load balancing and resource management. This abstraction ensures the application improves automatically as vendor implementations advance.
code_example: auto future = std::async(some_task); // Task-based, relies on scheduler optimization
practical_example: A developer writes a calculation module using `std::async`. When the application is run on a modern OS with an optimizing C++ library, the tasks are efficiently distributed across cores via work-stealing without the developer needing to write complex synchronization or load-balancing logic.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
